I farm a small 2.6 mu wheat-maize rotation field, and I have been doing this a long time, so I will keep the same steady system instead of trying anything complicated. Because I am 70 and my household is small, I will choose practices that are familiar, manageable, and dependable with my well irrigation. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer on before sowing with a moderate topdressing later, irrigate a few key times, and keep pest control simple. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what I would rely on for stable production, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate when it matters most, and avoid too many field operations. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me on this small farm and fits the wheat-maize system well. I am aiming for stable yield, not the highest possible yield, because at my age I care more about reducing risk and making sure the crop comes in smoothly.
